text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Washington warns French oil group Total against investing in Iran. The company is in talks with Iran involving a $2 billion investment to develop the South Pars gas field. The United States issued a law last year to slap sanctions on any foreign firm that invested $40 million or more in the oil sectors of Iran and Libya.

- Qatar firm on "me, myself and I" summit. Qatar said on Wednesday it is determined to host the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economic summit with Israel at the conference table. Qatar's powerful neighbour Saudi Arabia has advised Doha not to hold the summit at a time of stalled Arab-Israeli peace talks and said Riyadh would boycott the November event.
- Thirty channels for 10 dinars ($33). Kuwait's first cable television has been sactioned by ministries of information and commerce and is now awaiting clearance from a cabinet committee.
- Naval base for Coast Guard. A Kuwaiti firm last week signed a 30 million dinar ($99 million) deal to build the base.
- Jordanian security experts in Doha to protect the meetings of the MENA summit.
- Parliament's finance committee expressed surprise after a meeting on Wednesday at the government's failure to supply it with requested information on defence expenditures.
